fixed.how: The task's own change is now read again after the branch is brought up to date (rebase or merge) and before the push, in executeIn and in continueResolved. If nothing of the task's own is left, nothing is pushed. The new endUpToDate step closes the open pull request with one comment (closeEmptied, reason 'up_to_date': 'Brought up to date with main, this task's work no longer changes anything, so this pull request is closed. Its branch is kept.') and keeps its branch on the host. The task then fails in one sentence: '#4 no longer changes anything on main, so it was closed.', or 'main already has this change.' when no pull request was closed. In continueResolved the person's answer is marked used. emptiedSentence now takes a reason ('redone', 'empty' or 'up_to_date') instead of a boolean. Docs updated: ADR 0111 amendment point 1, capabilities.md, and two user-guide paragraphs (Redo, and 'A conflict the agent cannot resolve').

fixed.problem: Review blocking item 1: TM-4's new sentence ('#8 waits for the changes left in its task's folder: commit or remove them, or redo the task.') offered 'commit them' as a way out, which the code does not keep. The next check's rebuild resets the task branch to GitHub's copy (rebuildIn's createBranch(branch, origin/<branch>)). The person's commit then ends up on no branch, is never pushed, and the file disappears from the folder. This breaks design section 5 rules 8 and 9.

fixed.how:
New sentence (owedFolderSentence, 79 characters): '#8 waits for changes left in its task's folder: take them out or redo the task.' Each way out the sentence offers is now tested at the composed boundary, including what becomes of the person's change.
- Take them out (the file moved to a folder of the person's): the next poll rebuilds the branch, and the file is where the person put it, unchanged. Nothing of it reaches GitHub. The record then says what came of the rebuild: rebuilt without the closed pull request, it waits for the person's Merge again, with Merge offered and nothing merged.
- Redo: the run sets the changes aside and the folder is clean. The pull request holds only the task's file. The critic reviews it, and the record waits for the person's Merge again ('#N waits for you to merge it'). The earlier Merge is not carried over.
No logic changed: the 'commit' way out is simply no longer offered. The user guide no longer says 'your Merge goes on' (it does not after a rebuild without a closed dependency) and says not to commit in that folder. ADR 0111 point 5 and runtime.md give the reason.

not_done.problem: Keeping a commit a person makes in a done task's folder anyway (the reviewer's other option: the rebuild refuses, or keeps a local branch that is ahead of GitHub's)
not_done.why: The reviewer offered this as an alternative to fixing the sentence, not as a second requirement. I fixed the sentence and tested each way out it offers. A rebuild that refuses a branch ahead of GitHub's would also catch Forerunner's own local states: an unpushed base merge from a merge step that was cut short (merge.ts unpushedBaseMerge), or a rebuild whose push failed. Those would then wait forever with a sentence that blames the person's folder. Logged in new_problems with the reviewer's evidence.

All other assertions are unchanged, and two new tests now carry out the sentence's ways out.

new_problems: A commit a person makes in a done task's folder is dropped without a word when that branch is rebuilt. rebuildIn checks only for uncommitted changes, then runs createBranch(branch, origin/<branch>), so a local commit ends up on no branch and its files leave the folder. Reviewer's evidence: a scratch case in dependent-branches-merge.test.ts; result in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9d17d664-b8c3-5e0d-8f13-1f917f72dcc2/scratchpad/review-tm/exp-out.json and tm4-commit-case.ts.txt. This predates this area. The TM-4 sentence and the user guide no longer suggest committing, and the guide says not to. A real fix has to tell a person's commit apart from Forerunner's own unpushed base merge (merge.ts unpushedBaseMerge) and from a rebuild whose push failed; otherwise it holds the merge for ever under the folder sentence.

Before Merge is pressed, a row that owes a rebuild while its folder holds changes shows a plain Merge with no hint; the wait is only said after the click (sayOwedWait runs when a merge reaches the record). Seen on this bench at step 06 and in the review's step 06.

The Critic column shows a raw lowercase 'accepted' for a failed task and for a 'Mark done anyway' task (this bench: steps 18 and 25, 'Failed: #3 ...' and 'Done: accepted without review' with 'accepted' beside them). This predates this area: taskCheck returns null when the task is not done. It is for polish-screens or polish-words.

finishUnfinished edge cases, untested (from the review): (a) a resolved file with a real line starting '<<<<<<< ' or '>>>>>>> ' is read as unresolved for ever; (b) unstaged edits to other tracked files during the person's rebase make `rebase --continue` refuse, and must() throws, so the run fails with git's own text.
notes_for_other_areas:
polish-words, new or changed sentences to check against design section 5 (they replace or add to the fixer's list):
(1) loop/merge-mode.ts owedFolderSentence: '#8 waits for changes left in its task's folder: take them out or redo the task.' It replaces '... commit or remove them, or redo the task.' Do not bring back 'commit': the rebuild drops such a commit. The Tasks label OWED_FOLDER_LABEL 'Accepted · merge waits for you' is unchanged.
(2) pr-executor.ts emptiedSentence(pr, 'up_to_date', base): '#4 no longer changes anything on main, so it was closed.' and, with no pull request, 'main already has this change.' These are failed-task reasons, shown on the Tasks row as 'Failed: ...', on the failed card as 'What failed: ...' and in the Overview's last result.
(3) pr-executor.ts closeEmptied PR comment for 'up_to_date': 'Brought up to date with main, this task's work no longer changes anything, so this pull request is closed. Its branch is kept.'
(4) docs/user-guide.md: the owed-rebuild bullet (take them out / Redo / do not commit there; the row then says what came of the rebuild), one added sentence in the Redo paragraph ('Failed: #8 no longer changes anything on main ...; press Mark done anyway if that is what you wanted.') and one in 'A conflict the agent cannot resolve while it works' (a resolution keeping only main's side).
API change: emptiedSentence(prNumber: number | null, why: EmptiedWhy, base) now takes a reason, 'redone' | 'empty' | 'up_to_date', instead of a boolean. EmptiedWhy is exported from pr-executor.ts.

Behaviour other areas should know: PrTaskExecutor reads the task's own change again after it syncs with the base and before it pushes, in executeIn and in continueResolved. A branch with nothing left is never pushed, and its open pull request is closed (private endUpToDate). In continueResolved the 'I resolved it' answer is marked used on that path.
